note: Extensible archetype library (master prompt P2). Each archetype defines causal role, measurable state variables, transmission, monetization, lag, supply response, substitutes, invalidation, claim limit, required data, market applicability. Archetypes are MAPPED, not proven; activation formulas are frozen in R6 tournaments, never tuned on outcomes.

archetypes.transmission: demand > capacity -> allocation -> price
archetypes.monetization: price/ASP expansion at owner of constrained capacity
archetypes.invalidation: capacity additions announced + delivered; demand slows
archetypes.claim_limit: capacity data often company-reported; verify with industry sources

archetypes.transmission: qualification complete -> order ramp -> revenue
archetypes.claim_limit: qualification evidence often indirect (job posts, customer hints) — research-only until validated

archetypes.transmission: low yield -> constrained effective supply -> price
archetypes.claim_limit: yield rarely disclosed directly; infer from margin/output math

archetypes.transmission: lead time extends -> scarcity pricing -> allocation
archetypes.monetization: suppliers with short lead time gain share; owners of constrained parts raise price
archetypes.claim_limit: lead-time data from distributors is anecdotal unless systematic

archetypes.transmission: inventory below normal -> spot/contract price spike
archetypes.invalidation: inventory rebuild confirmed; demand rolls over
archetypes.claim_limit: official inventory lags; channel checks are noisy

archetypes.transmission: orders > output -> backlog builds -> pricing power
archetypes.monetization: backlog owner has revenue convexity to price
archetypes.claim_limit: backlog definitions vary; audit what is cancellable

archetypes.transmission: high utilization + demand growth -> price over volume
archetypes.claim_limit: utilization often estimated, not disclosed

archetypes.transmission: concentration + demand shock -> allocation
archetypes.claim_limit: concentration alone is not activation; needs demand trigger

archetypes.transmission: large customer ramp -> supplier revenue convexity
archetypes.invalidation: top customer cuts orders; dual-sourcing announced
archetypes.claim_limit: concentration cuts both ways — risk amplifier

archetypes.transmission: input shortage -> finished-good allocation
archetypes.claim_limit: dependency maps are incomplete without BOM data

archetypes.transmission: datacenter/industrial demand > grid supply -> power-priced allocation
archetypes.claim_limit: queue data is public but noisy; verify with utility filings

archetypes.transmission: logistics constraint -> delivered-cost spike -> basis dislocation
archetypes.claim_limit: freight is cyclical; structural vs transient must be separated

archetypes.transmission: approval -> market access -> revenue unlock
archetypes.claim_limit: binary event risk; size accordingly

archetypes.transmission: permit -> construction -> capacity
archetypes.claim_limit: permit timelines slip; use ranges not points

archetypes.transmission: skills shortage -> project delay/wage inflation
archetypes.claim_limit: job-posting evidence is research-only until validated

archetypes.transmission: financing cutoff -> forced asset sales/default -> supply exit
archetypes.claim_limit: distress timing is path-dependent

archetypes.transmission: low float + demand -> price overshoot
archetypes.monetization: early holders; also short-squeeze risk gauge
archetypes.claim_limit: float games are manipulation-prone — red-team mandatory

archetypes.transmission: borrow scarcity -> squeeze convexity
archetypes.monetization: long squeeze plays; short risk gauge
archetypes.claim_limit: squeeze timing is reflexive, not fundamental

archetypes.transmission: usage > capacity -> fee spike -> token value capture
archetypes.claim_limit: on-chain metrics are gameable; wash-filtered data required

archetypes.transmission: usage growth -> token demand (access) -> price
archetypes.monetization: token holders if value capture is real
archetypes.invalidation: usage decouples from token; unlocks flood supply
archetypes.claim_limit: most tokens fail the value-capture test — default skeptical

archetypes.transmission: AI/datacenter demand -> enterprise SSD/DRAM allocation -> ASP expansion -> margin convexity
archetypes.monetization: memory producers with constrained supply + mix shift to high-value customers
archetypes.invalidation: capacity adds delivered; ASP momentum reverses; inventory rebuilds
archetypes.claim_limit: NAND vs DRAM/HBM pools must NOT be conflated; separate products, capacity, economics

archetypes.transmission: specific grade/location shortage -> basis spike
archetypes.claim_limit: basis trades are capacity/credit intensive

archetypes.transmission: processing bottleneck -> product shortage despite feedstock availability
archetypes.claim_limit: spread data is public; edge is timing + structure

archetypes.transmission: reserve depletion -> forced devaluation/regime change
archetypes.claim_limit: intervention timing is political; size small

archetypes.transmission: collateral scarcity -> forced deleveraging -> dislocation
archetypes.monetization: cash-rich buyers of forced sales; tail hedges
archetypes.claim_limit: requires fast plumbing data; stale readings are dangerous

archetypes.transmission: positioning extreme -> hedging flows amplify/dampen moves
archetypes.monetization: structure selection (sell crowded tails, buy neglected convexity)
archetypes.claim_limit: dealer-position models are inference, not observation — validate before use
